 Gold rates in Delhi on November 4: 24,22 karat rates rise with Dhanteras two days away
 By Upstox News Desk 3 min read | Updated on November 04, 2026, 16:09 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 In Delhi, gold price was ₹13,980 a gram for 24 karat, ₹12,816 for 22 karat and ₹10,485 for 18 karat on November 4 at the time of writing.
 A showroom's price in Delhi can differ depending on the zone, the store and local supply. | Image: Shutterstock
 Gold rates in Delhi increased to ₹13,980 per gram for 24 karat and ₹12,816 per gram for 22 karat at the time of writing on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as jewellers across the city, including popular markets like Chandni Chowk and Karol Bagh, work through the last two days before Dhanteras. 
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 Ten grams of 24 karat gold works out to ₹1,39,800, while 22 karat, the grade most gold jewelleries are sold in Delhi, is ₹1,28,160. 18 karat gold is priced at around ₹10,485 a gram, or ₹1,04,850 for 10 grams.
 Purity Rate per gram Rate per 10 g Change from Nov 3 (per 10 gram) 
 24K (999) ₹13,980 ₹1,39,800 +₹270 (+0.19%) 
 22K (916) ₹12,816 ₹1,28,160 +₹250 (+0.20%) 
 18K (750) ₹10,485 ₹1,04,850 +₹200 (+0.19%) 
 Gold rates in Delhi on November 4; indicative, before making charges and GST 
 Buyers have until Friday, November 6, Dhanteras, and Sunday, November 8, Diwali, to finish their purchases, and shopkeepers in the city expect queues from Thursday morning.
 The fortnight has been choppy for gold rates . Delhi's 24 karat rate lost ₹5,060 per 10 grams, or 3.51%, in a single session on October 31, and Wednesday's ₹270 gain has clawed back only a fraction. However, against October's peak of ₹1,51,570, gold is still about ₹12,000 per 10 grams cheaper, a gap of nearly 8%. 
 Dealers attribute the slide to profit-booking after a record run and a firmer dollar overseas. MCX December gold settled at ₹1,39,452 per 10 grams on Tuesday, and spot gold edged higher in early Asian trade on Wednesday as the dollar softened. Most read the pre-Dhanteras bump as restocking rather than a new rally.
 Please note that the rates above are indicative. A showroom's price can differ depending on the zone, the store and local supply. So buyers should compare rates at several shops themselves instead of accepting the first figure offered. The final payment is also usually higher than the karat-based price, because making charges and 3% GST are added. For instance, a 10-gram 22 karat gold piece with 8% making charges attracts GST of ₹4,152, taking the total to about ₹1,42,565.
 Making charges, which may run from 6 to 18%, deserve as much comparison as the rate itself. Buyers should also ensure the jewellery carries a BIS hallmark and a six-digit HUID, and that the bill shows weight, purity, making charges and GST separately.
